title: Reupholstering the outside back and arms of a wing chair
subtitle: Replace the cover fabric on the three outer panels of a wing chair without disturbing the inside upholstery
excerpt: How to strip and recover the outside back and outside arm panels of a wing chair. Covers cutting out the old cover, cleaning the frame, cutting replacement fabric, slip-stitching or stapling the new panels in place, and finishing the bottom edge.
sourceNotes: Traditional upholstery construction practice. Period upholstery manuals (pre-1928 public domain). UK upholstery trade practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: The cover panel on the back face of an upholstered chair or sofa (the side the sitter does not lean against). The outside back is typically the last panel to be fitted and the first to be removed in a re-cover. It is tacked or slip-stitched to the top and side edges of the back frame and tucked under at the base.

The cover panel on the outer face of an upholstered arm. The outside arm sits between the seat rail (below), the arm rail (above), the back upright (behind), and the arm front scroll (in front). It is usually stapled or slip-stitched to the arm frame after all the inside panels are in place.

content.text: of a wing chair are the three outer covering panels. They are fitted last and wear most visibly. Replacing them without disturbing the inside upholstery is a practical re-cover option when the inside panels are still sound.

attrs.title: Before you start
attrs.body: Photograph the original chair from all angles before removing any fabric. The photographs show the original fitting sequence, how tucks were made at the corners, and how the bottom edge was finished. Use them as a reference throughout the re-cover.

content.text: Start with the outside back. Use the staple remover to lift all staples or the tack hammer to raise tacks around the perimeter of the outside back panel. Peel the panel free. Remove the two outside arm panels in the same way. Keep each removed panel whole: they are the patterns for the replacement panels. Do not attempt to remove any inside fabric or alter any filling or webbing under the inside panels.
Cut replacement panels from the old covers

Lay each stripped panel flat on the new fabric, right sides up, and add 30 mm turning allowance on all sides. Cut around the outside of the turning allowance. For a patterned fabric, position the outside back so the pattern is centred and matches the inside back pattern at the top edge. For the outside arms, match the pattern to the seat level if the fabric has a horizontal repeat.

Work one outside arm at a time. Lay the new panel over the outer face of the arm, grain running vertical, right side out. Fold the top edge over the arm rail and temporarily tack or staple it to the inside of the arm frame to hold the panel in place while working. Pull the bottom edge under the seat rail and staple it to the underside of the rail. Pull the back edge behind the back upright and fold under; slip-stitch it to the back edge of the inside arm using a curved needle and strong thread. Fold and tuck the front edge behind the arm scroll and staple to the front facing.

Tack or staple the top edge of the outside back panel to the inside face of the top back rail, folding the fabric over and down the back face. Pull the fabric down toward the base and tack at the sides. Use the upholstery regulator pushed through from the inside to move filling up behind any wrinkle that shows on the outside face. At the bottom, fold the fabric under and tack to the underside of the bottom rail.

Cut a piece of black bottom cloth (a lightweight hessian or cotton bottom fabric) slightly smaller than the underside of the seat. Fold the edges under by 15 mm and staple to the underside of the seat rail all the way around to cover all the raw edges and tacks.

attrs.symptom: Outside back panel shows diagonal wrinkles
attrs.cause: Panel not pulled equally from top and both sides simultaneously, causing the grain to pull off-square.
attrs.fix: Use the upholstery regulator to tease the panel straight under the fabric surface before final stapling. Always tack temporarily before final stapling so adjustments can be made.

attrs.symptom: Patterned fabric repeat does not match between inside back and outside back
attrs.cause: The inside back pattern centre was not measured before cutting the outside back.
attrs.fix: Measure the inside back pattern position before cutting the replacement outside back. The matching horizon is the seam line at the top of the outside back (where it joins the inside back at the top rail).
